classification.habitat: Dry to semi-dry tropical environments; commonly associated with other host plants through root connections
classification.distribution: Native to the Indian region and cultivated in several parts of India; authenticated provenance is important because sandalwood is commercially substituted and regulated in some contexts

identification.description: A small aromatic evergreen tree recognized by opposite leaves, small flowers and the characteristic fragrant heartwood of mature stems and roots.
identification.whole_plant: Small evergreen tree with slender branching crown; mature individuals develop a woody trunk.
identification.root: Woody roots; mature root heartwood may be aromatic. Detailed pharmacognostic characters require authenticated material.
identification.stem: Young branches are greenish; older stem develops grey-brown bark. Mature heartwood is yellowish to reddish-brown and characteristically aromatic.
identification.leaf: Simple, opposite, entire, smooth leaves, generally elliptic to lanceolate, with a glabrous surface.
identification.flower: Small flowers, initially pale green/yellowish and becoming darker reddish to purple-brown with age; borne in terminal or axillary cymose clusters.
identification.fruit: Small globose drupe, dark purple to nearly black when mature.
identification.seed: Single hard seed enclosed within the drupe.
identification.bark: Grey-brown outer bark; bark appearance alone is not sufficient for authentication of the medicinal heartwood.
identification_points: Small clustered flowers that darken with age
Characteristic aromatic heartwood in authenticated mature material
Differentiate true Santalum album from other aromatic woods and substitutes

modern_information.evidence_summary: Santalum album is primarily recognized for its aromatic heartwood and sandalwood oil. This educational dossier distinguishes traditional Ayurvedic use from modern clinical evidence and does not provide independent efficacy claims.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated material and appropriate regulated supply channels. Essential oils are concentrated preparations and should not be used as a substitute for traditional dosage/formulation guidance.

student.quick_revision: Chandana (Santalum album L., Santalaceae) is a small evergreen aromatic tree. The Ayurvedic record lists heartwood as the useful part, with Madhura-Tikta rasa, Sheeta virya and traditional use in Daha, Raktapitta, Trishna and Mutrakrichha.

practical_points: Observe opposite leaves and entire margins.
Examine mature fruit and authenticated heartwood where available.
Use a validated pharmacopoeial or herbarium reference for final identity.
